scenarios.title: A single timed event blocks the same time in the target
scenarios.expectedText: Target is busy on Tuesday 10:00 to 11:00 UTC and free in the rest of the week.

scenarios.title: A moved event frees the old time and blocks the new time
scenarios.expectedText: After the move the target is busy on Wednesday 14:00 to 15:30 UTC only; Tuesday is free.

scenarios.title: A deleted event frees its time and leaves other events alone
scenarios.expectedText: After the delete the target is free on Tuesday and busy on Thursday 09:00 to 09:30 UTC.

scenarios.title: A moved occurrence of a daily series blocks its new time, the others stay
scenarios.expectedText: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday are busy 09:00 to 09:30 UTC. Wednesday is busy 15:00 to 15:30 UTC and free at 09:00.

scenarios.title: A deleted occurrence of a daily series frees that day only
scenarios.expectedText: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday are busy 09:00 to 09:30 UTC. Thursday is free.

scenarios.title: An all-day event blocks its date in the time zone of the target
scenarios.expectedText: The Wednesday of the event is busy from midnight to midnight in the target zone, and the days next to it are free.

scenarios.title: Timed and all-day events over several days block every day they touch
scenarios.expectedText: Busy from Friday 14:00 UTC to Monday 09:00 UTC without a gap, and Tuesday to Thursday of the next week as full days.

scenarios.title: Daylight saving start: a series keeps its wall-clock time, a night event loses an hour
scenarios.expectedText: 09:00 Vienna is 08:00 UTC before the change and 07:00 UTC after it. The night event from 00:30 to 04:00 Vienna runs from 23:30 UTC to 02:00 UTC.
scenarios.local_limit: The simulation expands the series and applies the zone rules itself. Only a live run says something about a real calendar.

scenarios.title: Daylight saving end: a series keeps its wall-clock time, a night event gains an hour
scenarios.expectedText: 09:00 Vienna is 07:00 UTC before the change and 08:00 UTC after it. The night event from 00:30 to 04:00 Vienna runs from 22:30 UTC to 03:00 UTC.
scenarios.local_limit: The simulation expands the series and applies the zone rules itself. Only a live run says something about a real calendar.

scenarios.title: Events around midnight in the source zone keep their instants in a distant target zone
scenarios.expectedText: 23:30 to 00:30 Tokyo is 14:30 to 15:30 UTC, and 00:00 to 01:00 Tokyo on Thursday is 15:00 to 16:00 UTC on Wednesday. Nothing else is busy.
scenarios.local_limit: The simulation resolves the zones of the events itself. Only a live run says something about a real calendar.

scenarios.title: An event that does not block time leaves the target free
scenarios.expectedText: The free event never blocks the target. A busy event that turns free stops blocking it. The tentative event blocks.

scenarios.title: Cancelled and declined events do not block time
scenarios.expectedText: An event that the organizer cancels stops blocking, an event that the owner declined never blocks, and the witness event on Thursday stays busy.

scenarios.title: A private event blocks its time and shows no content
scenarios.expectedText: The target is busy on Tuesday 10:00 to 11:00 UTC, and no field of the block holds the title or the location.

scenarios.title: A rule that copies all details still shows nothing of a private event
scenarios.expectedText: The rule copies title, location and description. The block of the private Tuesday event holds none of them, and the block of the public Wednesday event holds its title.

scenarios.title: A working hours filter mirrors events that overlap the hours, at their full length
scenarios.expectedText: Hours are Monday to Friday 09:00 to 17:00 Tokyo, which is 00:00 to 08:00 UTC. Busy: 01:00 to 02:00 and the full overlapping event 07:30 to 09:00. Free: the event from 09:00 UTC, the event that ends exactly at 09:00 Tokyo, and the Saturday event.

scenarios.title: A working hours filter reads the date of its own zone, not the date in UTC
scenarios.expectedText: Hours are Monday to Friday 09:00 to 17:00 Tokyo. The event from Friday 23:30 UTC is Saturday morning in Tokyo, and the event from Saturday 23:30 UTC is Sunday morning there: both are free. The event from Sunday 23:30 UTC is Monday 08:30 to 09:30 in Tokyo, so it is busy at its full length.

scenarios.title: A buffer widens timed blocks on both sides and leaves all-day blocks alone
scenarios.expectedText: Buffers are 15 minutes before and 10 minutes after. Tuesday is busy 09:45 to 11:10. Two close events on Wednesday give one busy time from 09:45 to 12:10. Thursday stays one full day.

scenarios.title: With rules in both directions a block never comes back as a new block
scenarios.expectedText: Each calendar shows its own event and one block of the other event, after a settle time of 4300 s too. After the delete, both calendars are free on Tuesday and busy on Wednesday.
scenarios.local_limit: The simulation flags every block as a mirror itself. How the tool recognises its blocks in a real calendar stays unchecked.

scenarios.title: An event behind the end of the sync window stays out until the window reaches it
scenarios.expectedText: With a 14-day window the event on day 13 is busy and the event on day 20 is free. After eight days the window reaches day 20 and both are busy.

scenarios.title: A block that ends exactly at the start of the window goes when its event goes
scenarios.expectedText: An event ends at 00:00 UTC. Five minutes later, midnight has moved the window start to that end. While the event exists the target stays busy, and after the delete it is free.

scenarios.title: West of UTC an all-day event stays blocked after midnight UTC until its own day ends
scenarios.expectedText: It is still the day of the event in Los Angeles at 03:05 UTC the next day, so the block stays. After the delete that day is free.

scenarios.title: A block from before the window goes when its event goes after midnight
scenarios.expectedText: An event ends at 23:30 UTC. Five minutes after midnight, the window starts behind that end, and then the event is deleted. The target is free.

scenarios.title: A throttled source read waits for Retry-After, then the block appears
scenarios.expectedText: The source answers a read with 429 and Retry-After 120. For the next 110 seconds the tool makes no call to the source and the target stays free. Within two minutes after that the target is busy.
scenarios.local_limit: Both directions raise the read error of one calendar system. The error path of the other system stays unchecked.

scenarios.title: A throttled target write waits for Retry-After, then the block appears once
scenarios.expectedText: The target answers a write with 429 and Retry-After 180. For the next 170 seconds the tool makes no call to the target. Within two minutes after that the target is busy, with one block.

scenarios.title: One failed write in a batch comes back with the next cycle, without duplicates
scenarios.expectedText: The target refuses one write of a batch of three. Within 70 minutes all three times are busy, each with one block.

scenarios.title: A paused source keeps its blocks, and a reconnect catches up on what changed
scenarios.expectedText: The source token is refused. While paused, the Tuesday block stays and the new Wednesday event does not arrive, even after the Tuesday event is deleted. After the reconnect only Wednesday is busy.

scenarios.title: Disconnecting the source account frees the target
scenarios.expectedText: After the source account is disconnected, the target is free in the whole week.

scenarios.title: Disconnecting the target account removes its blocks and keeps its own events
scenarios.expectedText: After the target account is disconnected, its own Wednesday event remains and the block on Tuesday is gone.
scenarios.local_limit: The simulated calendar goes with the account. From then on the check reads a snapshot from before the last alarm. That alarm only forgets the account, and a delete in it would stay unseen.

scenarios.title: The title of an event never reaches the target at the default detail level
scenarios.covers: data that must not reach the target
scenarios.expectedText: A block exists, and none of its fields holds the title of the event. This scenario checks data only, not times.

scenarios.title: The location of an event never reaches the target at the default detail level
scenarios.covers: data that must not reach the target
scenarios.expectedText: A block exists, and none of its fields holds the location of the event. This scenario checks data only, not times.

scenarios.title: The description of an event never reaches the target at the default detail level
scenarios.covers: data that must not reach the target
scenarios.expectedText: A block exists, and none of its fields holds the description of the event. This scenario checks data only, not times.

scenarios.title: The attendee of an event never reaches the target at the default detail level
scenarios.covers: data that must not reach the target
scenarios.expectedText: A block exists, and none of its fields holds the attendee of the event. This scenario checks data only, not times.
